title: Video shows fight before FDLE agent shot and killed man in SW Miami-Dade
summary: Heart-stopping cellphone video appears to capture the fight before a Florida Department of Law Enforcement agent shot and killed a man in southwest Miami-Dade. Deputies responded to the shooting shortly after 9 a.m. Thursday in the area of Southwest 157th Avenue and Southwest 140th Street. Investigators said the agent was inside his vehicle when a man who was standing in the street approached and started hitting the vehicle’s window. The agent exited and there was a physical altercation, and at one point the other man threw the agent to the ground and got on top of him, officials said. Video taken by a driver appears to show that fight between the two men as cars honk in the busy roadway. It also shows the moment one of the men picks up the other and slams him to the ground, then gets on top of him. One of the men can be heard yelling, “Help, help, help! He’s got a gun.” The footage shakes as the driver recording appears to get out of their car, also warning, “Hey, he got a gun.” Then, a shot goes off. The sheriff’s office said it was the FDLE agent who opened fire, shooting the man who had slammed him to the ground. Witness Julyana Adam said she was inside her home when she heard a single gunshot. “All I hear is ‘help, help he has a gun,'” Adam said. “Then a gunshot goes off.” A Miami Police officer who was in the area and Miami-Dade deputies responded and gave the person lifesaving efforts, but they were pronounced dead at the scene. On Friday, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office identified the man who was killed as 28-year-old Daniel Thomas Shand. Daniel Thomas Shand FDLE said the agent was on duty at the time of the shooting, but haven’t said what he was doing in the neighborhood. The agent suffered minor injuries during the altercation and was taken to a local hospital for treatment, FDLE said. He was placed on administrative leave as is standard procedure. Adam said she soon learned who died. “The landlord, he stepped out and he’s like, ‘that’s one of ours,'” she said. “That’s when I was like, you know, that’s my neighbor.” A normally quiet neighborhood was shattered by violence. Adam, like many of her neighbors, wants to know why. “It was scary… to hear them arguing in the beginning and then to hear somebody say ‘help, help’ and I can’t do much other than like look out the window,” she said. “Whatever happened there, shouldn’t have happened, or escalated to that level.” The sheriff’s office’s Homicide Bureau is investigating at the request of FDLE, officials said.

title: Trump says he's banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
summary: President Donald Trump said Friday that he had banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over what he called their “constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.” In a Truth Social post Friday afternoon , Trump said media outlets “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the Untied States.” Trump also warned “other outlets” would “follow” but did not specify which. It was not immediately clear if journalists for those news outlets had been removed from the White House grounds as of Friday afternoon. CNN, MS Now and Politico did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The First Amendment guarantees freedom of the press and the outlets are likely to challenge any ban in court. CNN reported that its team remained at the White House as of Friday afternoon. Trump, responding to a reporter in the Oval Office shortly after announcing the ban, said the new policy was the result of “cumulative stories over the last few years.” He did not specify a particular news report, and a White House spokesperson referred NBC News to the president’s spoken comments. The move is the latest in Trump’s ongoing efforts to punish news organizations and broadcasters for their coverage. Shortly after taking office, Trump banned the Associated Press from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events after it declined to acknowledge his call to change the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. The AP filed suit and the case is ongoing. Trump has also taken legal action against outlets including the BBC, New York Times and Wall Street Journal after they published unfavorable reports. The suits against the Times and Journal were subsequently dismissed. The BBC has filed to get Trump’s suit against it tossed. Democrats denounced Friday’s move. “This is yet another attack on the First Amendment from a president who knows he and his party of bootlickers are deeply unpopular,” Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker wrote on X. “Donald Trump can’t hide from his failing record, so he’s banning journalists he doesn’t like to keep you from hearing about it.” The Freedom of the Press Foundation, a nonprofit founded in the wake of the Wikileaks scandal in 2012, also criticized Trump’s announcement. “It’s difficult to imagine a more blatant violation of the First Amendment than Trump banning news outlets from the People’s House for criticizing the government,” a spokesman said. “It’s also hard to imagine a dumber move. The historically unpopular president has been retaliating against the press for years, but it hasn’t helped him.” During his first administration, Trump banned CNN’s then-chief White House correspondent Jim Acosta from the executive mansion. CNN sued, and the White House subsequently restored Acosta’s credentials. Friday’s bans come as Trump’s approval ratings have sagged and with Democrats gaining a polling edge in many pivotal midterm races that could see Republicans lose control of Congress. He has at times taken particular issue with reporting on the Iran war, writing on Truth Social earlier in September that coverage of ammunition shortages was “actually treasonous.

title: Ex-Miami Hurricanes star Mark Pope arrested, accused of pistol-whipping woman
summary: Former Miami Hurricanes star Mark Pope was arrested on armed robbery and other charges after he was accused of pistol-whipping a woman, records showed. The 27-year-old was booked into Miami-Dade’s Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center Thursday and also faces an aggravated battery charge, records show. According to an arrest report, Pope and the victim knew each other through their neighborhood and had agreed to meet at a park on Southwest 218th Street. While there, they got into a dispute in the victim’s vehicle before Pope pulled out a gun and hit her in the face with it then forcibly took her phone from her hand, the report said. The victim fled from the car and went to a nearby gas station where she called police. Pope was found a short time later and taken into custody before he was booked into jail. During a Friday bond court appearance attended by Pope’s parents, his defense attorney argued for a reasonable bond, telling a judge Pope works for a security company and has no prior arrests. “He’s a graduate of the University of Miami, was a standout on the University of Miami football team, was a standout on the football team at University of Massachusetts, this has to be some misunderstanding with some lady friend,” attorney Robert Pelier said. The judge gave Pope house arrest with a GSP monitor and told him to stay away from the alleged victim. Pope, a wide receiver who grew up in Miami, attended Miami Southridge High School before going to UM beginning in 2018. He played in 34 games for the Hurricanes before transferring to Jackson State and then Massachusetts. In 2024, he signed with the Toronto Argonauts of the Canadian Football League, but he was released in 2025.
